Energy transition

Carbon Fee

San Francisco's coal plant has years left in it, but you pay a fee on its emissions. How soon can you afford to replace it?

Play Carbon Fee↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location
San Francisco, California
Starts in
2020
Your term
12 years

Your starting point

Your utility enters 2020 with an aging coal plant, a gas plant and a limited construction budget. Both plants pay a fee on emissions. The fee goes up in January 2024.

Your customers still need electricity while you build. If you close the coal plant first, check how much of that demand your gas plant can cover.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Work out what coal costs

    Add the carbon fee to the cost of running each plant. Coal emits more per unit of electricity, so the higher fee hits it harder.

  2. 02

    Time the retirement

    Check your replacement's opening date before taking the old plant out of service.

  3. 03

    Set a rate customers will pay

    Raising prices can help pay for construction. Watch how many customers stay as their bills change.
